title: R439 single-copy interleaving reduces scatter from 94 to 88 ADDs
body:
PR2356 leaves open whether another retained total benefits from taps interleaved with the fixed R439 target undo. This supplies a column-0 witness: ten taps replace sixteen reads, reducing the complete scatter from **94 to 88 ADDs** and the full PR1062 word from **11,067 to 11,061 ADDs**. All 306 undo gates remain charged; nine rank-seven COPY/ERASE pairs, one live copy slot, the 2,911 ordered MOVEs and rank mass 5,129 are unchanged.

This is a finite construction outside PR2279's split-ideal optimum, not a contradiction of that result. The reverse positive majorant rises slightly to 5,026,856; the inherited local/nine-stage guards still use 95/181 bits under 104/192 caps. No optimality, supplier adoption or new kappa is claimed.

The package checks every one of 661 arbitrary dirty input columns in both directions. A separate mathematical agent's set-valued interpreter and independently computed rational frame ranks reproduce all 13,990 literal records exactly. Registered CPython3.12 replay passes with nine primary and five independent rejection controls, equivalent-presentation controls, real entry-point source/witness/receipt corruptions, guard-removal sensitivity and read-only Git-free relocation. Normal and optimized checks pass; primary replay also passes CPython3.14. Selected-record integrity is unchanged. No hosted-CI pass is claimed.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-single-copy-interleaving
```

Native parser/address execution of target undo inside a live COPY, native 5/9/11-stage replay, whole-call hosting/invoice, physical recursive scratch, all-size/compiler/precision/tape and outer assembly remain separate. PR2373's native replay covers a different non-interleaved word.

Base `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision4. Exact input and predecessor pins, proof, fixed witness, receipt, attribution and open next questions are in the new package. Credit Sagar Thakrar's PR1062/2115, Charles Bethin's PR2279, Sricharan Vagvala's PR2356 model and checker methodology, Gareth Davidson's PR915/2373, and the retained helper-star, B-circuit, frame, PR589/555, interface and exporter lineage. Prepared by Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human or formal-kernel review. Apache-2.0.
